newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Volvo sees strength in share redemption.
newsitem.headline: Volvo sees strength in share redemption.

text.p: Swedish automotive group AB Volvo said on Wednesday its plan to redeem one in every 20 shares is a way of strengthening the company.
"We see the share redemption plan as a way of strengthening the company," Jan Engstrom, the company's financial director, told a news conference.
"It is also a solution while awaiting a possibility to buy back shares."
Swedish companies are currently not allowed to buy back shares, but regulations might be revised.
Engstrom also saw share redemption as more beneficial tax wise for shareholders than a cash pay out.
"It is also positive for Volvo because it gives us an opportunity to issue new shares if we need new capital," Engstrom said.
He added the offer will contain "a reasonable premium" but could not specify how large it would be. The details in the share redemption plan will be presented before March 19.
